sanskrit: ke cin mokṣaṃ praśaṃsanti ke cid yajñaphalaṃ dvijāḥ vānaprasthāśramaṃ ke cid gārhasthyaṃ ke cid āśritāḥ
english: Some praise liberation, O brāhmaṇas, and some the fruit of sacrifice; some cleave to the forest-hermit's order, and some to the life of the householder.

sanskrit: rājadharmāśrayaṃ ke cit ke cid ātmaphalāśrayam gurucaryāśrayaṃ ke cit ke cid vākyaṃ yam āśrayam
english: Some take refuge in the duty of kings, and some in the fruit that pertains to the self; some rest in service to a teacher, and some in this saying or that as their support.

sanskrit: mātaraṃ pitaraṃ ke cic chuśrūṣanto divaṃ gatāḥ ahiṃsayā pare svargaṃ satyena ca tathā pare
english: Some, by waiting in service upon mother and father, have gone to heaven; others have reached heaven through non-injury, and yet others through truth.

sanskrit: āhave 'bhimukhāḥ ke cin nihatāḥ svid divaṃ gatāḥ ke cid uñchavrataiḥ siddhāḥ svargamārgasamāśritāḥ
english: Some, struck down while facing the foe in battle, have gone to heaven; others, perfected by the vow of gleaning, have taken the road that leads to heaven.

sanskrit: ke cid adhyayane yuktā vedavrataparāḥ śubhāḥ buddhimanto gatāḥ svargaṃ tuṣṭātmāno jitendriyāḥ
english: Some, devoted to study and intent on the Vedic vows, the pure and the wise, content in spirit and masters of their senses, have gone to heaven.

sanskrit: ārjavenāpare yuktā nihatānārjavair janaiḥ ṛjavo nākapṛṣṭhe vai śuddhātmānaḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ
english: Others, joined to uprightness though slain by men who walked crookedly, the upright and pure of soul, are established upon the vault of heaven.

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhair loke dharmadvārair anāvṛtaiḥ mamāpi matir āvignā meghalekheva vāyunā
english: Thus, by the many and unbarred gateways of dharma in the world, my own mind too is set astir, like a streak of cloud scattered by the wind.

sanskrit: atithir uvāca upadeśaṃ tu te vipra kariṣye 'haṃ yathāgamam guruṇā me yathākhyātam arthatas tac ca me śṛṇu
english: The guest said: I shall give you instruction, O brāhmaṇa, in keeping with tradition, even as it was expounded to me by my teacher; hear it from me in its true meaning.

sanskrit: yatra pūrvābhisargeṇa dharmacakraṃ pravartitam naimiṣe gomatītīre tatra nāgāhvayaṃ puram
english: There, where in a former creation the wheel of dharma was set in motion, in Naimiṣa on the bank of the Gomatī, stands a city named after the Nāga.

sanskrit: samagrais tridaśais tatra iṣṭam āsīd dvijarṣabha yatrendrātikramaṃ cakre māndhātā rājasattamaḥ
english: There, O bull among the twice-born, sacrifice was offered by all the gods together, there where Māndhātā, best of kings, surpassed even Indra.

sanskrit: kṛtādhivāso dharmātmā tatra cakṣuḥśravā mahān padmanābho mahābhāgaḥ padma ity eva viśrutaḥ
english: There has taken up his dwelling a righteous soul, the great Cakṣuḥśravas, the lotus-naveled and greatly blessed one, renowned simply as Padma.

sanskrit: sa vācā karmaṇā caiva manasā ca dvijarṣabha prasādayati bhūtāni trividhe vartmani sthitaḥ
english: He, O bull among the twice-born, by speech and by deed and by mind, gladdens living beings, standing firm upon the threefold path.

sanskrit: sāmnā dānena bhedena daṇḍeneti caturvidham viṣamasthaṃ janaṃ svaṃ ca cakṣurdhyānena rakṣati
english: By conciliation, by gift, by sowing division, and by force—these four means—he guards both the people set against him and his own folk, watching over them with the meditation of his eye.

sanskrit: tam abhikramya vidhinā praṣṭum arhasi kāṅkṣitam sa te paramakaṃ dharmaṃ namithyā darśayiṣyati
english: Approaching him in due form, you may ask what you desire; and he, without falsehood, will reveal to you the highest dharma.

sanskrit: sa hi sarvātithir nāgo buddhiśāstraviśāradaḥ guṇair anavamair yuktaḥ samastair ābhikāmikaiḥ
english: For that Nāga is a host to all, deeply versed in wisdom and the sacred lore, endowed with every excellence that one could wish, none of them deficient.

sanskrit: prakṛtyā nityasalilo nityam adhyayane rataḥ tapodamābhyāṃ saṃyukto vṛttenānavareṇa ca
english: By nature ever pure as water, ever delighting in study, joined with austerity and self-restraint, and of conduct in no way wanting.

sanskrit: yajvā dānaruciḥ kṣānto vṛtte ca parame sthitaḥ satyavāg anasūyuś ca śīlavān abhisaṃśritaḥ
english: A performer of sacrifice, delighting in giving, patient, established in the highest conduct, truthful in speech, free from envy, virtuous, and a sure refuge.

sanskrit: śeṣānnabhoktā vacanānukūlo; hitārjavotkṛṣṭakṛtākṛtajñaḥ avairakṛd bhūtahite niyukto; gaṅgāhradāmbho 'bhijanopapannaḥ
english: He eats only the food that is left over, and is agreeable in his speech; eminent in benevolence and uprightness, he knows what has been done and what is left undone. He bears no enmity, is devoted to the welfare of all beings, and is endowed with lineage pure as the waters of Gaṅgā's deep pools.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca atibhārodyatasyaiva bhārāpanayanaṃ mahat parāśvāsakaraṃ vākyam idaṃ me bhavataḥ śrutam
english: The brāhmaṇa said: Like the lifting of a great burden from one who labors beneath too heavy a load, this consoling word of yours have I heard.

sanskrit: adhvaklāntasya śayanaṃ sthānaklāntasya cāsanam tṛṣitasya ca pānīyaṃ kṣudhārtasya ca bhojanam
english: As a bed to one weary from the road, as a seat to one weary of standing, as water to the thirsty and food to one afflicted with hunger;

sanskrit: īpsitasyeva saṃprāptir annasya samaye 'titheḥ eṣitasyātmanaḥ kāle vṛddhasyeva suto yathā
english: as the gaining of a thing long desired, as food coming to a guest at the proper season, as a son born to an aged man who has yearned for him in his time;

sanskrit: manasā cintitasyeva prītisnigdhasya darśanam prahrādayati māṃ vākyaṃ bhavatā yad udīritam
english: as the sight of a dear and loving one whom the mind had been longing for—so does the word you have spoken gladden me to the heart.

sanskrit: dattacakṣur ivākāśe paśyāmi vimṛśāmi ca prajñānavacanād yo 'yam upadeśo hi me kṛtaḥ bāḍham evaṃ kariṣyāmi yathā māṃ bhāṣate bhavān
english: As one to whom sight has been given, I now look upon the open sky and ponder it. Since this instruction has been given me out of words of wisdom, I shall indeed do exactly as you tell me.

sanskrit: ihemāṃ rajanīṃ sādho nivasasva mayā saha prabhāte yāsyati bhavān paryāśvastaḥ sukhoṣitaḥ asau hi bhagavān sūryo mandaraśmir avāṅmukhaḥ
english: Stay here this night with me, O good one; at daybreak you shall go your way, refreshed and well rested. For yonder the blessed Sūrya, his rays grown faint, sinks with his face turned downward.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tatas tena kṛtātithyaḥ so 'tithiḥ śatrusūdana uvāsa kila tāṃ rātriṃ saha tena dvijena vai
english: Bhīṣma said: Then, having received that hospitality, the guest, O slayer of foes, passed that night, so it is told, together with that brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: tat tac ca dharmasaṃyuktaṃ tayoḥ kathayatos tadā vyatītā sā niśā kṛtsnā sukhena divasopamā
english: And as the two of them conversed on this and that matter touching dharma, the whole of that night passed pleasantly away, like a day.

sanskrit: tataḥ prabhātasamaye so 'tithis tena pūjitaḥ brāhmaṇena yathāśaktyā svakāryam abhikāṅkṣatā
english: Then at the hour of dawn the guest was honored, to the best of his power, by that brāhmaṇa who longed to accomplish his own purpose.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa vipraḥ kṛtadharmaniścayaḥ; kṛtābhyanujñaḥ svajanena dharmavit yathopadiṣṭaṃ bhujagendrasaṃśrayaṃ; jagāma kāle sukṛtaikaniścayaḥ
english: Then that brāhmaṇa, knower of dharma, his resolve in dharma now fixed, taking leave of his kinsfolk, set out in due time toward the abode of the lord of serpents, as he had been directed, single in his resolve upon the good.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sa vanāni vicitrāṇi tīrthāni ca sarāṃsi ca abhigacchan krameṇa sma kaṃ cin munim upasthitaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: As he journeyed on by stages, passing through wondrous forests and sacred fords and lakes, he came at length upon a certain sage.

sanskrit: taṃ sa tena yathoddiṣṭaṃ nāgaṃ vipreṇa brāhmaṇaḥ paryapṛcchad yathānyāyaṃ śrutvaiva ca jagāma saḥ
english: Of him the brāhmaṇa duly inquired after the Nāga, as that other brāhmaṇa had directed; and having heard, he went on his way.

sanskrit: so 'bhigamya yathākhyātaṃ nāgāyatanam arthavit proktavān aham asmīti bhoḥśabdālaṃkṛtaṃ vacaḥ
english: Reaching the Nāga's dwelling as it had been described, that man of discernment uttered, adorned with a courteous greeting, the words: "Here I am."

sanskrit: tatas tasya vacaḥ śrutvā rūpiṇī dharmavatsalā darśayām āsa taṃ vipraṃ nāgapatnī pativratā
english: Then, hearing his words, the wife of the Nāga, fair of form, cherishing dharma and faithful to her lord, showed herself to that brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: sā tasmai vidhivat pūjāṃ cakre dharmaparāyaṇā svāgatenāgataṃ kṛtvā kiṃ karomīti cābravīt
english: Devoted to dharma, she paid him honor in due form, and having welcomed the newcomer with words of welcome, she said: "What may I do for you?"

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca viśrānto 'bhyarcitaś cāsmi bhavatyā ślakṣṇayā girā draṣṭum icchāmi bhavati taṃ devaṃ nāgam uttamam
english: The brāhmaṇa said: I am rested, and I have been honored by you with gentle speech, gracious lady. I wish to behold that godlike one, the most excellent of Nāgas.

sanskrit: etad dhi paramaṃ kāryam etan me phalam īpsitam anenārthena cāsmy adya saṃprāptaḥ pannagālayam
english: This indeed is my highest errand, this the fruit I desire; and for this purpose have I today come to the abode of the serpent.

sanskrit: nāgabhāryovāca ārya sūryarathaṃ voḍhuṃ gato 'sau māsacārikaḥ saptāṣṭabhir dinair vipra darśayiṣyaty asaṃśayam
english: The Nāga's wife said: Noble sir, he has gone to draw the chariot of Sūrya for his month-long term of service; in seven or eight days, O brāhmaṇa, he will without doubt show himself to you.

sanskrit: etad viditam āryasya vivāsakaraṇaṃ mama bhartur bhavatu kiṃ cānyat kriyatāṃ tad vadasva me
english: Let this be known to your noble self—the cause of my husband's absence. Whatever else there may be to be done, tell me, and let it be done.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca anena niścayenāhaṃ sādhvi saṃprāptavān iha pratīkṣann āgamaṃ devi vatsyāmy asmin mahāvane
english: The brāhmaṇa said: With this very resolve, O virtuous one, have I come here; awaiting his return, O lady, I shall dwell within this great forest.

sanskrit: saṃprāptasyaiva cāvyagram āvedyo 'ham ihāgataḥ mamābhigamanaṃ prāpto vācyaś ca vacanaṃ tvayā
english: And when he has duly arrived, you are calmly to announce that I have come here; my arrival should be made known, and these my words spoken to him by you.

sanskrit: aham apy atra vatsyāmi gomatyāḥ puline śubhe kālaṃ parimitāhāro yathoktaṃ paripālayan
english: I too shall dwell here, on the fair bank of the Gomatī, awaiting the appointed time, eating but sparingly, abiding as has been said.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tataḥ sa vipras tāṃ nāgīṃ samādhāya punaḥ punaḥ tad eva pulinaṃ nadyāḥ prayayau brāhmaṇarṣabhaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Then that brāhmaṇa, having reassured the Nāga's wife again and again, that bull among the twice-born went away to that very bank of the river.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atha tena naraśreṣṭha brāhmaṇena tapasvinā nirāhāreṇa vasatā duḥkhitās te bhujaṃgamāḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Now, O best of men, those serpents grew distressed because that ascetic brāhmaṇa was dwelling there without taking any food.

sanskrit: sarve saṃbhūya sahitās tasya nāgasya bāndhavāḥ bhrātaras tanayā bhāryā yayus taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ prati
english: All the kinsmen of that Nāga, gathering together—his brothers, his sons, and his wife—went up to that brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: te 'paśyan puline taṃ vai vivikte niyatavratam samāsīnaṃ nirāhāraṃ dvijaṃ japyaparāyaṇam
english: They beheld him on a lonely stretch of the bank, that brāhmaṇa of steadfast vow, seated and fasting, intent upon his recitation of prayer.

sanskrit: te sarve samabhikramya vipram abhyarcya cāsakṛt ūcur vākyam asaṃdigdham ātitheyasya bāndhavāḥ
english: They all came forward and, honoring the brāhmaṇa again and again, the kinsmen of their host spoke these unequivocal words.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭho hi divasas te 'dya prāptasyeha tapodhana na cābhilaṣase kiṃ cid āhāraṃ dharmavatsala
english: This is now the sixth day since you came here, O treasury of austerity, and yet you crave no food at all, O cherisher of dharma.

sanskrit: asmān abhigataś cāsi vayaṃ ca tvām upasthitāḥ kāryaṃ cātithyam asmābhir vayaṃ sarve kuṭumbinaḥ
english: You have come to us, and we have presented ourselves before you; the duty of hospitality must be fulfilled by us, for we are all householders.

sanskrit: mūlaṃ phalaṃ vā parṇaṃ vā payo vā dvijasattama āhārahetor annaṃ vā bhoktum arhasi brāhmaṇa
english: A root, or a fruit, or a leaf, or milk, O best of the twice-born, or grain to sustain you—deign to eat something, O brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: tyaktāhāreṇa bhavatā vane nivasatā satā bālavṛddham idaṃ sarvaṃ pīḍyate dharmasaṃkaṭāt
english: Because you, who have forsaken food, dwell here in the forest, all of us, young and old alike, are tormented by this strait of conscience.

sanskrit: na hi no bhrūṇahā kaś cid rājāpathyo 'nṛto 'pi vā pūrvāśī vā kule hy asmin devatātithibandhuṣu
english: For there is none among us who has slain an embryo, none disloyal to the king, none false of word, nor any who eats before the gods, guests, and kinsmen are served in this our house.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca upadeśena yuṣmākam āhāro 'yaṃ mayā vṛtaḥ dvirūnaṃ daśarātraṃ vai nāgasyāgamanaṃ prati
english: The brāhmaṇa said: By your own counsel I have undertaken this manner of fasting, until the return of the Nāga, for ten nights less two.

sanskrit: yady aṣṭarātre niryāte nāgamiṣyati pannagaḥ tadāhāraṃ kariṣyāmi tannimittam idaṃ vratam
english: If, when the eight nights have passed, the serpent should not come, then I shall take food; for his sake alone is this my vow.

sanskrit: kartavyo na ca saṃtāpo gamyatāṃ ca yathāgatam tannimittaṃ vrataṃ mahyaṃ naitad bhettum ihārhatha
english: You ought not to grieve; go your way as you came. This vow of mine is for his sake, and you should not break it here.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tena te samanujñātā brāhmaṇena bhujaṃgamāḥ svam eva bhavanaṃ jagmur akṛtārthā nararṣabha
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus dismissed by the brāhmaṇa, those serpents went back to their own dwelling, their errand unaccomplished, O bull among men.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atha kāle bahutithe pūrṇe prāpto bhujaṃgamaḥ dattābhyanujñaḥ svaṃ veśma kṛtakarmā vivasvataḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Then, when many days were fulfilled, the serpent arrived, having been given leave, his service to Vivasvat done, and came to his own abode.

sanskrit: taṃ bhāryā samabhikrāmat pādaśaucādibhir guṇaiḥ upapannāṃ ca tāṃ sādhvīṃ pannagaḥ paryapṛcchata
english: His wife came forward to attend him with the rites of washing his feet and the rest; and the serpent questioned that virtuous lady so endowed with merits.

sanskrit: api tvam asi kalyāṇi devatātithipūjane pūrvam uktena vidhinā yuktā yuktena matsamam
english: Have you, O gracious one, in the worship of gods and guests, kept faithfully to the rule laid down of old, fitting and worthy of me?

sanskrit: na khalv asy akṛtārthena strībuddhyā mārdavīkṛtā madviyogena suśroṇi viyuktā dharmasetunā
english: Surely you have not, with a woman's softness of mind, grown lax through any unfulfilled task, O fair-hipped one, nor, through separation from me, fallen away from the bridge of dharma?

sanskrit: nāgabhāryovāca śiṣyāṇāṃ guruśuśrūṣā viprāṇāṃ vedapāraṇam bhṛtyānāṃ svāmivacanaṃ rājñāṃ lokānupālanam
english: The Nāga's wife said: For pupils, service to the teacher; for brāhmaṇas, the completion of the Veda; for servants, the word of their master; for kings, the protection of the world;

sanskrit: sarvabhūtaparitrāṇaṃ kṣatradharma ihocyate vaiśyānāṃ yajñasaṃvṛttir ātitheyasamanvitā
english: the deliverance of all beings is here declared to be the duty of the kṣatriya; for the vaiśyas, the carrying out of sacrifice, conjoined with hospitality;

sanskrit: viprakṣatriyavaiśyānāṃ śuśrūṣā śūdrakarma tat gṛhasthadharmo nāgendra sarvabhūtahitaiṣitā
english: service to brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas is the work of the śūdra; and the householder's duty, O lord of serpents, is the seeking of the welfare of all beings.

sanskrit: niyatāhāratā nityaṃ vratacaryā yathākramam dharmo hi dharmasaṃbandhād indriyāṇāṃ viśeṣaṇam
english: Restraint in food at all times, the practice of vows each in its order—for dharma, by its very kinship with dharma, is the disciplining of the senses.

sanskrit: ahaṃ kasya kuto vāhaṃ kaḥ ko me ha bhaved iti prayojanamatir nityam evaṃ mokṣāśramī bhavet
english: "Whose am I? Whence am I? Who am I? Who here could be mine?"—he whose mind is ever bent on this inquiry into purpose becomes thereby one set upon the path of liberation.

sanskrit: pativratātvaṃ bhāryāyāḥ paramo dharma ucyate tavopadeśān nāgendra tac ca tattvena vedmi vai
english: Fidelity to her husband is declared the highest dharma of a wife; and that, O lord of serpents, I know in its very truth, from your own teaching.

sanskrit: sāhaṃ dharmaṃ vijānantī dharmanitye tvayi sthite satpathaṃ katham utsṛjya yāsyāmi viṣame pathi
english: How, then, should I—who know dharma, while you who are ever constant in dharma still stand by me—forsake the good road and walk upon a crooked path?

sanskrit: devatānāṃ mahābhāga dharmacaryā na hīyate atithīnāṃ ca satkāre nityayuktāsmy atandritā
english: The observance of dharma toward the gods, O greatly blessed one, has not been neglected; and in the welcoming of guests I have been ever diligent and unwearied.

sanskrit: saptāṣṭadivasās tv adya viprasyehāgatasya vai sa ca kāryaṃ na me khyāti darśanaṃ tava kāṅkṣati
english: For it is now seven or eight days since a brāhmaṇa came here; nor does he disclose his errand to me, but only longs for the sight of you.

sanskrit: gomatyās tv eṣa puline tvaddarśanasamutsukaḥ āsīno ''vartayan brahma brāhmaṇaḥ saṃśitavrataḥ
english: On the bank of the Gomatī he sits, eager for the sight of you, that brāhmaṇa of stern vow, reciting the sacred word.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tv anena nāgendra sāmapūrvaṃ samāhitā prasthāpyo matsakāśaṃ sa saṃprāpto bhujagottamaḥ
english: By him, O lord of serpents, I was earnestly told, with gentle and conciliatory words: "He, the best of serpents, when he has returned, is to be sent to my presence."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā mahāprājña tatra gantuṃ tvam arhasi dātum arhasi vā tasya darśanaṃ darśanaśravaḥ
english: Having heard this, O greatly wise one, you ought to go to him there; or grant him the sight of you, O you whose very seeing is renowned.

sanskrit: nāga uvāca atha brāhmaṇarūpeṇa kaṃ taṃ samanupaśyasi mānuṣaṃ kevalaṃ vipraṃ devaṃ vātha śucismite
english: The Nāga said: Now then, what manner of one in a brāhmaṇa's form do you take him to be—a mere mortal brāhmaṇa, or perhaps a god, O you of pure smile?

sanskrit: ko hi māṃ mānuṣaḥ śakto draṣṭukāmo yaśasvini saṃdarśanarucir vākyam ājñāpūrvaṃ vadiṣyati
english: For what mortal, O illustrious one, desiring to behold me and longing for my sight, would be able to speak words framed almost as a command?

sanskrit: surāsuragaṇānāṃ ca devarṣīṇāṃ ca bhāmini nanu nāgā mahāvīryāḥ sauraseyās tarasvinaḥ
english: Among the hosts of gods and demons, and among the divine seers too, O lovely one, surely we Nāgas, sprung from Surasā, are mighty in valor and swift in strength;

sanskrit: vandanīyāś ca varadā vayam apy anuyāyinaḥ manuṣyāṇāṃ viśeṣeṇa dhanādhyakṣā iti śrutiḥ
english: and we are worthy of homage and bestowers of boons, even when we follow in another's train; over men in particular we are lords of wealth—so runs the sacred saying.

sanskrit: nāgabhāryovāca ārjavenābhijānāmi nāsau devo 'nilāśana ekaṃ tv asya vijānāmi bhaktimān atiroṣaṇaḥ
english: The Nāga's wife said: In all candor I judge that he is no god, O eater of the wind; one thing only do I perceive of him—he is full of devotion, though quick to wrath.

sanskrit: sa hi kāryāntarākāṅkṣī jalepsuḥ stokako yathā varṣaṃ varṣapriyaḥ pakṣī darśanaṃ tava kāṅkṣati
english: For he, desiring nothing but his one errand, like the cātaka-bird that craves water and longs for rain, that bird in love with rain, so longs for the sight of you.

sanskrit: na hi tvā daivataṃ kiṃ cid vivignaṃ pratipālayet tulye hy abhijane jāto na kaś cit paryupāsate
english: For no divine being, troubled at heart, would wait thus upon you; one born of equal lineage does not pay court to another.

sanskrit: tad roṣaṃ sahajaṃ tyaktvā tvam enaṃ draṣṭum arhasi āśāchedena tasyādya nātmānaṃ dagdhum arhasi
english: Therefore, casting off your inborn anger, you ought to grant him sight of you; by cutting off his hope this day, you ought not to scorch your own self.

sanskrit: āśayā tv abhipannānām akṛtvāśrupramārjanam rājā vā rājaputro vā bhrūṇahatyaiva yujyate
english: A king, or a king's son, who fails to wipe away the tears of those who come to him in hope, is bound by the guilt of slaying an embryo itself.

sanskrit: maunāj jñānaphalāvāptir dānena ca yaśo mahat vāgmitvaṃ satyavākyena paratra ca mahīyate
english: From silence comes the winning of the fruit of knowledge, and from giving, great renown; by truthful speech one gains eloquence, and is exalted in the world beyond.
